The three primitives—AST originality enforcement, hypothesis-factor alignment, and complexity control—are designed to prevent overfitting and crowding. AST-based similarity penalizes reuse of prior structures, ensuring novelty. Hypothesis alignment ensures that new factors are grounded in domain knowledge rather than noise. Complexity control balances expressiveness with interpretability. These primitives form a dual system: one that enforces structural diversity and another that enforces semantic coherence. Failure modes include misalignment of hypotheses with data, overpenalization of complex but valid signals, and insufficient novelty enforcement leading to redundant factor generation. The system’s robustness depends on dynamic calibration of α weights and continuous validation against out-of-sample performance.
